Gripper prototype 2: motion

Monorail beam on the middle forearm pipe (racks on both sides, MGN12 rail on top); pistol grip with a spray-bottle trigger at the top, 18–30 mm clear of the grip for your fingers. CDX-3R, Fusion model, 18 Oct 2026.

  • Stowed over the forearm, behind the wrist
  • Slides 250 mm forward on the rail; a spring plunger (pull knob) snaps in and holds it there
  • The trigger hangs from the top of the grip (index + middle finger); squeezing it opens the claws, letting go a spring closes them
  • Pull the plunger knob sideways: the head glides back slowly (damper on the left rack)
  • The right rack is free for a motor pinion later

Review fixes

Your four review points, each now caught by a test in design_rules.py. The tests were written first and failed on the old model, then the model was fixed. They run with every check and commit.

TestWhat it checksOld modelNow
Floating partsEvery part touches another and links back to the rail baseCable housing touched nothingPass
Drive chainTrigger → wire → pusher → drive pin → gear R → gear L → claws all touch (head slid out)Trigger → wire 20.8 mm apart; wire → pusher 9.5 mmPass
Gear meshesGears have teeth and sit at their partnerDamper gear: 3 faces, no teethPass
StrengthSlender printed parts under a hard squeeze, safety factor ≥ 3Drive pin 2.1 (printed, upright); trigger horn 0.8Pass: pin steel 13, horn 4.3

Fitting the trigger cable

You asked how the wire gets through solid material. In the earlier version it couldn't: the arm's channel turned 90° inside the plastic. Now the only walled-in stretches are short and straight, and a new test (cables) checks exactly that: it failed on the old route and passes now.

  1. Hook the cable's barrel nipple behind the trigger's horn and drop the wire into the horn's slot (open at the top).
  2. Push the wire straight through the 4.5 mm wall into the housing; lay the housing into the side pocket against the wall.
  3. Bend the housing round its loop and seat its other end on the cable stop at the front of the arm.
  4. Push the wire through the stop and the pusher lever's hole.
  5. Slide on the screw nipple, take up the slack, tighten its grub screw. That also sets how early the claws start to open.
